pillar_reactions.evidence: Not the flagship pillar but its group-product equivalent, described as 'a full setup already from workouts that you can start following to build a whole foundation, and then after that, have like a monthly challenge.' The prospect's reaction to the whole description was a single 'No, yeah, I mean, that makes sense.'
Not raised at all on this call. It was presented as part of the flagship on the previous day.

Presented in its reduced group form - the Thursday live session, a place to ask questions about nutrition, training and accountability, and form feedback from 'Trevor, Caden, or someone else that's been doing kettlebells for a long time'. Accepted without questions, which is notable given that on the prior call accountability was the pillar he reacted to most strongly.

anchors.raw: Even my credit score is at a spot where I'm not going to get, you know, more than 1500 probably dollars.
anchors.note: The decisive number. He went away and checked, and the answer is that no financing route reaches $6,000. Combined with $150-175 of available cash, this is a hard ceiling rather than a negotiating position, and it sits below even the $1,200 group product in a single payment.

anchors.raw: It's way more than I thought something like that would be for six months. I personally think it's too much, but I believe in it.
anchors.note: Distinct from affordability and more useful. Having slept on it and discussed it with his partner, he concluded the price is wrong for what is offered, while still wanting the programme. That is a pricing signal rather than a qualification signal.

anchors.raw: we're just on the edge with the new house and stuff. And we have to buy a storage unit... we're saving up for a vacation, so, across the country, and he has to work seven days a week
anchors.note: The household is already running at capacity on a new house, a storage unit and a holiday fund, with the partner working seven days a week to sustain it. Any Primal spend competes directly with that.

anchors.raw: Absolutely supports me. We want this, you know, it would be something he'd be interested in, too.
anchors.note: The partner conversation produced enthusiasm rather than resistance, and Josh is interested for himself. The blocker is genuinely money and not permission, which is the more workable of the two - and it points at an unserved couples proposition, the second time that has surfaced in this batch.

unmet_demand.want: To know the price before investing two calls' worth of time. He raised it unprompted and apologetically: 'I know there's a reason you don't know the money first, but I don't like going this far and knowing, and then doing this to y'all.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing in the funnel discloses a price. This is the second prospect in two days, independently and in different circumstances, to raise the same complaint - the other one ended his call over it. Taken together they are strong evidence that late price disclosure is costing qualified time on both sides.

unmet_demand.want: A route to the coaching that fits inside $150-175 a month and a $1,500 credit ceiling
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The group product at $200 a month is close but still above his stated maximum, which is why the rep tried to move him from $175 to $200. There is no financing option, no lower tier and no third-party lender, so a prospect with extremely high intent sits just outside every available price point.

unmet_demand.want: Certainty that money spent on the group product is not wasted if he later affords the one-to-one
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered on the call with a promise that it would be credited toward the one-to-one at any future date, 'even if it takes longer than the six months' - but no such policy appears anywhere else in the corpus, no terms were stated and nothing was put in writing. The demand is real and the answer given is unverified.
